findings.claim: The creation and signature rows determine whether they are the last row by checking only `!showExecutionRow`, without checking whether the new Safenet row will also render. For a transaction still collecting signatures that already has a Safenet check, this causes the last signature (or creation) row to be marked last incorrectly, so its connector line is omitted and the Safenet row appears disconnected from the timeline.

The component duplicates the API's logic for choosing the attestation event (oracle first, plain as fallback) instead of sharing it with `packages/store/src/safenet/safenetCheckApi.ts`. The code comment claims it links to the same event the API verifies, but nothing enforces that the two implementations stay in sync, so a future change to one side could make the link point to a transaction other than the one actually verified.

This new component lacks a `.stories.tsx` file, which the project's AGENTS.md conventions require for new components; its five statuses and the new `actor`/`iconColor` props on `AuditRow` are consequently only exercised in tests, not visible in Storybook.

The new tests only cover the Safenet row alongside a normal execution row and do not cover a transaction still awaiting signatures that also has a Safenet row, which is the exact scenario in which the timeline connector bug occurs.

The comment describing the block-header read as costing 'one RPC per settled check' is inaccurate: `blockTimeMs` actually runs on every poll that sees an attestation event, including polls every 6 seconds while waiting for verification and every refetch after the 300-second cache expires, so the comment should be corrected or the read limited to only when status is `BENIGN` or `MALICIOUS`.
When the block-header read fails, the reader retries each RPC endpoint in turn, which delays the verdict for that poll.
`NEXT_PUBLIC_SAFENET_EXPLORER_URL` is read here but is missing from `apps/web/.env.example`, even though the diff documents every other Safenet environment variable there.
